memos.risk:
Recommendation: refuse. Do not buy at any size.

The brief shows a coin that is almost certainly not a fair-launch memecoin. One buyer group controls 99.85% of early buying (top-5 share 0.9985, bundle share 1.0), the sell-to-buy ratio in the first two minutes is 0.0009, and the curve shows completer share near 2.87 with only 1 buyer. That looks like a single operator's bundle, not organic demand. Operator-backed coins have been roughly break-even on average, but this profile is extreme, and the exit liquidity is the problem: with a 0.04% drawdown and 26 sellers in the last 15 minutes against 29 buyers, any coordinated unwind lands on the remaining holders.

Also, the ticker and name imitate a sovereign or institutional fund. Treat that as a red flag, not a signal.

If the desk insists on a position anyway, the minimum-risk version is $5, a 20% stop, and a 15-minute hold. But the expected value after a 1.4-5.1% round trip is negative, so I'd skip it entirely.
memos.scout:
The brief shows real activity, but almost all of it is concentrated in a few wallets. Top-5 buyers hold 99.85% of early buy volume, the bundle share is 1.0, and 1,003 SOL came in from 19 buyers in the first two minutes after graduation. That is the operator pattern, not organic demand. Over the last 15 minutes, 26 of 29 buyers were also sellers, and net flow is only +5.3 SOL on 11 SOL bought, so the recent "volume" is largely the same wallets trading against each other. The price is flat over 30 minutes, with a 0.04% drawdown from the high, which could mean support but could equally mean an operator holding the line before distributing.

The strongest honest argument is that the coin is alive, has a 30-minute return of +5%, and has a $8.4M market cap with 1,100 SOL of pool depth, so exits should be possible at a 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost. I can't build a case that broader demand will persist in the next 30-60 minutes. Nothing in the brief shows buyers outside the operator cluster, and an operator-backed coin is roughly break-even on base rates before accounting for fees. Recommendation: skip.
memos.skeptic:
Most likely loss path: insider distribution. The first two minutes after graduation show 1,002.87 SOL bought by 19 wallets, with the top 5 buyers holding 99.85% of that volume and a launch bot present. The bundle share is 1.0 and top3 share 1.0, so supply sits with a tiny cluster. Sell-to-buy in the first two minutes is 0.0009, meaning almost nobody sold early, which is classic for an operator holding a concentrated position they can exit at will.

Recent flow is thin and fading: 11.08 SOL bought vs 5.78 SOL sold in the last 15 minutes, 29 buyers against 26 sellers, net flow of only 5.31 SOL on a $2,050 volume print. A 0.96% move over 15 minutes is smaller than the 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost, so even a flat-to-up drift loses money after fees. The 8.4M market cap on a 1,101 SOL pool is also thin relative to the operator's stake, so a single large exit would hit price hard. A $20 entry here is paying fees to become exit liquidity.
